races.name: Why Settle Technology AI Adoption EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton 2yo Series Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed 2yo from Charlie Johnston's yard, rated 106 after placing four times over 7f on Good ground — the step up to 1m½f is the key question, and she must be taken on trust over a trip she has never tackled; David Egan takes the ride and she is likely to race prominently as natural to her style, giving her every chance to dictate on Good To Soft.

runners_data.name: Trumpety Trump
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 2yo has form figures of 3-4 over 6f on Good ground, so both trip and surface are unproven territory; Rhys Elliott claims 5lb which helps on weight, but as a hold-up horse in a three-runner race run at a controlled pace, she will need a significant uptick in performance at a longer distance to get involved.

runners_data.name: Nice Neasy Does It
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's debutant is a complete unknown — no racecourse experience, no public form, and her going preference is entirely uncharted; David Allan is an experienced handler of unknown quantities and Easterby's juveniles on debut are worth monitoring (5/84 in 14 days), but the lightly raced flag demands significant caution in any tactical assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Pikachu is the only confirmed pace-setter in a field of three, and with no rival likely to push forward and challenge for the lead, she can dictate a completely uncontested, measured gallop over this testing 1m½f at Hamilton on Good To Soft ground. Trumpety Trump is a hold-up type who will naturally sit last, while Nice Neasy Does It is an unknown quantity on debut but gives no front-running profile signals. With one horse controlling tempo at her own pace, the race is set to be run at an even, sustainable rhythm where the leader can conserve energy through the early stages before being asked to quicken in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile — horses who can travel close to a gentle pace and respond when the tempo increases, rather than those needing a searching gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pikachu Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pikachu bowls along at her own comfortable tempo and the field fails to close in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Pikachu dictates every yard from the front without a single rival threatening to rattle the gallop, arriving at the turn with reserves intact and able to quicken away in the straight; this suits a horse racing prominently on easy terms over a distance that is an extension of her recent 7f form on similar ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nice Neasy Does It possesses natural talent that overcomes any positional uncertainty, tracking the pace and producing a potent finish.
scenarios.body: A debut runner from Tim Easterby's yard with no form line is an unknown quantity, but if she has been schooled to race prominently or mid-division she could take advantage of an honest if gentle pace and reel in a tiring Pikachu; the Good To Soft surface suits a well-bred debutant who hasn't been exposed to softer ground before.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and Trumpety Trump delivers a sustained late run that catches Pikachu on the line.
scenarios.body: Trumpety Trump has run creditably in 6f contests on Good ground and a step up in trip may release more stamina, allowing a hold-up effort to come with one sustained challenge on the home turn; however, a slow pace set by Pikachu is precisely the worst scenario for a horse needing to be produced late, making this difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Pikachu fails to see out the longer trip and the field finishes in a heap with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: A distance of 1m½f is new territory for Pikachu whose form is entirely over 7f, and if she ties up in the final furlong the race opens up for whichever rival has been most economically ridden; the small field of three means any of the trio could benefit from an unexpected collapse, though this is a low-probability outcome given the controlled nature of the likely pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Nice Neasy Does It's debut behaviour at the start dictates the race shape — a slow break or reluctance to settle could gift Pikachu an even more uncontested lead.
Pikachu has never raced beyond 7f and Hamilton's stiff, undulating track over 1m½f on Good To Soft could expose any stamina limitations in the final furlong, watch for signs of tying up.
Trumpety Trump's hold-up style in a three-runner field means she is entirely dependent on a strong pace collapsing Pikachu — monitor whether Elliott opts to adapt and track the leader instead.

The official going is recorded as Good To Soft despite the race header stating Soft — confirm the precise strip condition before the off as any further overnight rain could materially alter stamina requirements and favour hold-up types.

races.name: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here, and Jim Goldie's five-year-old will stride into an uncontested lead on good-to-soft; her recent Hamilton record and similar-going stats are modest (0W0P on sim-going) but she rarely gets as soft a lead as she will today over an ideal trip.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old has genuine in-form claims off a sequence that includes two wins and two seconds — however, her natural hold-up style cannot be fully executed here given the cluster of closers, and she will need to race closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers her chance slightly.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell has a strong 14-day strike rate and Callum Rodriguez is a confident booking; this filly has won twice over 8f on good and stays 8f well, and while stepping to 9f (1m1f) may suit her galloping action, she needs to produce a strong finish from rear to count.

runners_data.name: Foxy Night
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over for John Butler, who has six winners from 24 recent runners; course form (hg:p — she has worn headgear) is noted and she has placed on soft/standard ground previously, though her last five runs at 7-8f leave a question mark over whether 9f stretches her stamina sufficiently.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's filly posted her sole win over 8f on soft ground at Ayr, making today's conditions directly applicable; Sam James rides for a yard with eight winners from 32 runners in the last fortnight, and if she replicates that soft-ground form she becomes a serious runner in any scenario where closers can get through.

runners_data.name: Wild Dahlia
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old is a genuine prominent type with a win and a second from her last four starts, and headgear (hg:t — tongue-tie) suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up; her one run on soft was modest (4th over 7f) but she should cope with today's ground at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Sharona
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi's mare is returning from a 401-day absence and her entire recent form is built over distances of 10-18f — stepping back sharply to 9f looks an uncomfortable fit, and her natural stamina-dependent style, pushed closer to the pace by the redistributed mapping, makes her a major query on both counts.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's veteran seven-year-old has been running consistently in the frame (three 3rds, a 2nd in her last five) and is fresh off a 10-day turnaround; she will press forward as a prominent type and her consistency at 8-9f on good ground makes her a reliable each-way player if the race unfolds at a steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's three-year-old arrives on the back of a three-timer and has won her last three over 8-10f on good ground; Shane Gray rides and she is dropping significantly in class, with the going and trip well within her scope — her sim-going record is modest but her recent form trajectory is the most compelling in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is almost certain to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on good-to-soft ground over 1m1f at Hamilton. Behind her, Wild Dahlia and Second Fiddle will press forward into prominent positions, but neither has the gate speed or the inclination to challenge Krissy for the lead, meaning the pace is hers to set and she can regulate it entirely to her own rhythm. The hold-up contingent — Porth Eilian, Foxy Night, Thankfully, Polygram and Sharona — will be funnelled into midfield and rear positions, with Polygram and Sharona specifically tagged as redistributed types who would naturally race further back but cannot find that space given the volume of hold-up horses in this field. A sustainable, uncontested pace on a galloping track like Hamilton, on ground that rewards stamina over sprint, sets this race up squarely for a prominent or pace-pressing runner who can travel close to Krissy and pounce without needing to make up excessive ground in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krissy Controls, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy leads unchallenged and sets a steady-to-moderate tempo, allowing prominent types to travel comfortably just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Krissy dictates throughout and the moderate gallop on good-to-soft means stamina is tested but not brutally so, benefiting runners who have tracked her and can quicken from short range in the Hamilton straight. Wild Dahlia and Second Fiddle, poised just behind, get the ideal race-shape and can challenge without having to find an extra gear from an impossible position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Krissy Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Krissy becomes truly soporific and the field never quickens sufficiently to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Krissy, unchallenged and relaxed through the early and middle stages, conserves enough energy to find a second wind in the straight and the pack, having dawdled, cannot generate a meaningful late run. This suits a front-runner who has won over this sort of trip on good ground and simply never faces a serious challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and burns off the prominent runners, leaving a late run viable from the rear.
scenarios.body: With the field compressing in the straight and the frontrunners tiring, a hold-up horse who has settled off the pace and conserved energy could arrive late with a powerful run. Thankfully and Porth Eilian, both suited to longer distances and capable of finishing strongly, are best placed to exploit this shape — though Polygram's redistributed position means it may struggle to replicate a true hold-up role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the ground deteriorates further or riding tactics misfire and the race becomes a war of attrition throughout.
scenarios.body: A grinding, stamina-sapping affair with no clear winner emerging until deep in the straight would scramble the expected order, potentially promoting a horse with proven soft-ground form or fresh legs. Foxy Night's course experience and Sharona's stamina credentials offer marginal claims, though Sharona's 401-day absence makes this a significant ask.

watchPoints.text: Krissy has no rival for the lead and will dictate the entire tempo — if she finds a comfortable rhythm and is never headed, watch whether Wild Dahlia and Second Fiddle can maintain contact through the middle mile to mount a challenge, because if they drop away the front-runner's chance grows substantially.

Polygram and Sharona are both redistributed hold-up horses who cannot get their natural position — watch whether they get any room to challenge from behind in the straight or are trapped in a traffic pocket through the final two furlongs, as their best efforts depend on clear passage they may not find.

Saxon Grace's three-race winning streak over 8-10f on good ground is the standout form line, but her going stats on similar ground (4/15, 0W0P) raise a caution — watch how she handles the softer conditions specifically, as a reversal of her recent form trajectory is possible if the ground doesn't suit.

Thankfully's sole win came on soft at Ayr over 8f — today is 9f on good-to-soft at Hamilton, the closest comparable conditions she has faced, and how she travels in the early stages under Sam James will signal whether she can reproduce that form or whether the step up in trip blunts her finishing kick.

races.name: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid form over longer trips in good-to-soft conditions (1W4P from 15 similar-going runs), but a three-runner field with an uncontested leader makes finding a true pace to close into very difficult; Shane Gray will need a strong gallop to set up a late run that his style demands.

runners_data.name: Flagbearer
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained three-year-old with only one run to his name (4th, 8f, good), stepping sharply up to 1m3f in softer conditions — Cieren Fallon's booking adds confidence but the complete unknown running style and lightly raced flag make him the race's biggest variable; class on paper (OR 120) vastly outstrips his rivals but it must be treated with caution given the single data point.

runners_data.name: Lord d'Or
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old has a consistent placed record (three second-place finishes) stepping up to 1m3f for the first time, and as the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field on going he handles, Callum Rodriguez can dictate every yard and set whatever tempo suits; the question is whether his OR of 82 can withstand the theoretical class of Flagbearer in the home straight.

races.paceDynamic: Lord d'Or is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the off in this three-runner field over 1m3f on good to soft ground at Hamilton, with no rival likely to challenge him for the lead. Flagbearer is a lightly raced unknown (style tagged U) who could sit anywhere, while Nakassama is a hold-up type who will settle in the rear by default in such a small field. With Lord d'Or able to dictate entirely unchallenged, he will control tempo, preserve energy, and make the race a test of attrition rather than pace — a scenario that historically suits the horse on the front end at Hamilton's flat, galloping track. This race shape strongly favours a pace-compliant, front-running profile: Lord d'Or sets his own fractions, and unless his class deficit against Flagbearer proves decisive, the race is his to lose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lord d'Or Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lord d'Or dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and neither rival can pick him up in the straight.
scenarios.body: Lord d'Or settles into his natural front-running role, controlling the fractions on soft ground over 1m3f, and simply sustains his effort to the line; Nakassama's hold-up style leaves him with too much ground to make up in a slowly run race with only three runners.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Flagbearer's Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If Flagbearer, despite lightly raced profile, possesses enough raw class on an OR of 120 to reel in Lord d'Or in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cieren Fallon tracks Lord d'Or comfortably from second position and produces Flagbearer's superior class rating in the closing stages, overhauling the leader; the significant OR differential (120 vs 82) is the decisive factor if Flagbearer handles the softer ground and step up in trip from his single run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Nakassama Sweeps Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to soften Lord d'Or late, allowing Nakassama to close ground from the rear.
scenarios.body: Nakassama has proven form over longer trips in similar going and has a win and four places from 15 comparable runs, suggesting stamina; however, in a small field where the pace is likely to be moderate, a sustained run from the back is a tall order with only three rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates further or any runner fails to handle conditions, leading to an atypical messy outcome.
scenarios.body: With the going officially good to soft and a very small field, any horse failing to act on the surface could gift the race to whichever rival handles it best; this is a low-probability scenario given all three are tagged going OK, but soft-ground risks are never zero in Scotland in these conditions.

watchPoints.text: Flagbearer's OR of 120 dwarfs the field — if Cieren Fallon times a move on the turn into the straight, Lord d'Or's lead could be swallowed quickly despite the controlled gallop.
Nakassama's hold-up style is fundamentally compromised by the three-runner field and likely moderate pace — watch whether Shane Gray adjusts tactics and sits closer than usual to compensate.
Lord d'Or has not run beyond 10f previously — the step to 1m3f on soft ground is an untested stamina query that could see him tie up late if he's gone too hard early.
Hamilton's 1m3f is a flat, galloping track that suits front-runners who can control fractions — Lord d'Or's tactical advantage here is greater than course records alone might suggest.

All three runners are cleared going OK on good to soft, but the going report confirms good to soft across all distances today — no degradation concern, though any late rain should be monitored given Nakassama's better soft-ground profile.

races.name: Scullion Law Lanark Silver Bell Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: El Burhan
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course record of adapting to soft-ground routes and a recent win over 10f on soft; George Boughey's yard is in fine form (4 wins from 22 over 14 days) and Pat Cosgrave is a sharp tactical rider — the 11f trip at Hamilton suits his grinding style perfectly.

runners_data.name: Yabher
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse trained by the powerful William Haggas yard, but whose recent form at a mile is clearly short of his best — soft-ground form is present but his last five runs are all over 10f on good and two of those produced double-figure finishes, raising a significant stamina question at 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Strassia
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up stayer who has won over 1m4f on soft and placed at 1m7f on soft, making her the most credible deep closer in the field on a ground basis; 330 days off is the major unknown and she has been absent since a sixth on good — fitness on return is the only caveat worth naming.

runners_data.name: Noble Horizon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with five recent starts over 10f on good at Newmarket, making this a clear step up in trip and a significant change in ground — Callum Rodriguez rides and the Oli Rix yard has a modest 14-day record (0 wins from 2); trip and going are both untested here.

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the Balding yard who has a PU in his most recent start and has produced five consecutive finishes outside the first three; Andrew Balding has been firing at 7/56 over 14 days, but Teumessias Fox himself is short of form and his soft-going record is limited.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has raced exclusively over 2m+ recently, suggesting this 1m4f trip could be too sharp; Shane Gray takes the ride for the James Owen yard and while his soft-ground exposure is reasonable, his finishing positions (8-14-6-8-6) show a horse that rarely threatens at the business end.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won three of his last five and holds a recent second over 12f on good — the step to soft at 1m4f at Hamilton is new ground, but Sam James is a canny handler of prominent types and this could be a yard trying to win a heritage handicap in good form (though T14 shows 0/10).

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race and the pivot on which the entire pace map turns; David Egan can control tempo entirely without pressure, and while his five recent runs are all over 10f on good, his age (3) and lighter weight (128lbs) are assets — the risk is whether he has the stamina to sustain his lead over 1m4f on this ground.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: A prominent racer in outstanding form, having won three of his last five including back-to-back wins over 12f on both good and soft — Daniel Muscutt continues the partnership and the Fanshawe yard carries a 5/22 14-day strike rate; the soft-going win at 12f is particularly relevant here.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from the David O'Meara yard with a second over 13f on soft in his recent history, giving him both trip and going credentials; Mark Winn takes the ride and while Ashnak's overall form is mixed (including a seventh and an eighth), the soft-ground run at 13f shows he stays and handles cut.

runners_data.name: Evaluation
runners_data.note: A true hold-up stayer — an eight-year-old who has finished in the frame over 16f multiple times on soft and good — but mapped to midfield here because the field is saturated with hold-up horses; his natural position would be last or near-last, and the controlled pace set by Evanesco means he is unlikely to land the late run his form pattern demands.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Has winning form at a mile but his last five runs include a 19th and an 11th on good, suggesting significant inconsistency; Lauren Young (5lb claim) takes the ride for Jim Goldie and while this is a step down in distance from some runs, his actual run style at the rear of the field is genuine — he just needs a pace scenario that will not materialise today.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Has won twice at around 11f on good to soft ground and shows a third at 12f on good, giving him some staying credentials; naturally a hold-up horse who would want to race last and deliver a late surge, but that tactic is undermined by the projected steady tempo — Joanna Mason rides for the Charlie Johnston yard, which has a solid 14-day record (5/35).

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose most recent win was over 11f on good — the experience at 12f on heavy is missing, though he did finish second over 10f on good recently; Andrew Mullen rides for Iain Jardine, who is 4/30 over 14 days, and Tiernan's redistribution to midfield accurately reflects that he won't find the deep-closing run his style demands today.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Has winning form over 17f on good and 11-12f on good, suggesting stamina is not an issue, and the three-pound claim from Amie Waugh is a bonus in a handicap; ran just five days ago (fitness is there), but as a natural hold-up horse racing in a pace-starved race, his closing run will be blunted — the Goldie yard (4/38, 14 days) is in decent nick.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Egan can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Soft ground over 1m4f at Hamilton. The prominent horses — El Burhan, Noble Horizon, Spioradalta, Salamanca City and Ashnak — will compete to sit just behind Evanesco, creating a compact early order but no real pressure on the leader. This controlled pace over a staying trip on soft-ish ground is a classic set-up that rewards horses who can travel close to the pace and quicken in the straight rather than those who need a breakneck gallop to close from far back. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Evaluation, Altareq, Elsass, Tiernan and Letsbefrank are all genuine come-from-behind horses but are mapped into midfield given the congestion; of these, Evaluation and Letsbefrank are most likely to find a position further back than their mapped slot, but none will get the truly fast pace they need to close from deep. **Tactical verdict: prominent racers who can sit second or third on the fence and produce a sustained galloping challenge through the straight are most favoured; pure hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged by the absence of genuine pace.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco sets a measured, uncontested lead and the race is run at a steady honest gallop that suits grinding prominent types.
scenarios.body: Evanesco dictates from the front and the race is essentially a procession until the home straight, where the best-placed prominent horses peel off and grind him down or match him; horses travelling smoothly just off the pace through the race's early stages arrive full of running at the two-furlong pole. Salamanca City and El Burhan, both in-form prominent racers with soft-ground form, are ideally placed to attack off this shape, with Spioradalta and Noble Horizon also in the mix.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Evanesco Steals It Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop is never truly challenged and Evanesco's rivals leave the leader's advantage unaddressed until too late.
scenarios.body: Evanesco bowls along in front at a comfortable tempo and, with no one willing to apply early pressure in a big field on a track that already favours the front rank, he simply finds enough in the straight to hold on; the slow pace paradoxically removes the prominent horses' advantage by meaning they all arrive together with little room to manoeuvre. David Egan's tactical awareness and Charlie Johnston's strong recent trainer form make this a live option if the chasing pack misjudges the fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Grinding Test, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates or rides significantly softer than reported, turning the race into a true stamina slog.
scenarios.body: A slower, heavier surface kills the rhythm of one-paced prominent types and rewards the horse with the deepest reserves; Strassia, who has winning form over soft ground at staying distances and ran a strong third at 1m7f on soft, could emerge as a progressive stayer with the conditions clearly in her favour. Yabher, a William Haggas-trained hold-up horse who has won twice at a mile and a quarter, also merits respect if ground-induced attrition opens the race up from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected pace develops and genuine hold-up horses benefit from a stronger gallop than Evanesco alone can manufacture.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on the redistributed hold-up horses — Evaluation, Elsass, Tiernan and Letsbefrank — actually landing in natural rear positions and being delivered late into a collapsed front, which is structurally unlikely given the absence of genuine pace to collapse; even Letsbefrank, a recent winner who is lightly campaigned for a six-year-old, would need a materially faster tempo than this race shape projects to get competitive. The probability is deliberately low because the horses who would win this shape are racing out of role and the dominant pace figure is set up to make their task harder, not easier.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of El Burhan, Spioradalta or Salamanca City attempt to push up and sit directly behind Evanesco early — if two or three prominent horses fight for the same position on the rail, it will create early friction and could compress the pace unexpectedly.

Monitor Evanesco's early sectionals through the first half-mile: if David Egan senses no pressure and deliberately slows the gallop below an honest staying tempo, the entire field bunches and the race becomes a 2f sprint, which dramatically flattens the form book.

Strassia's 330-day absence is a significant flag — if she shows any sign of rustiness or is ridden with extreme caution by David Nolan in the early stages, she may fail to travel close enough to the pace to land her usual late run even if the ground suits.

Letsbefrank ran just five days ago — watch in the paddock for any signs of tiredness or dullness in coat; a horse running that freshly in a heritage handicap over 1m4f on soft ground is worth monitoring for early and late energy levels.

Noble Horizon has run all five recent starts over 10f at Newmarket on good ground — this is a significant switch in both trip (plus 4f) and going; if he shows any hesitancy in the soft early on or Callum Rodriguez has to push him along to maintain position, his chance diminishes rapidly.

races.name: Acrisure Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Germanic
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer for Julie Camacho who has won twice at the trip and sits well OR=91 off the pace; jockey Ryan Sexton rides and the Good to Soft is fine, though his sim-going record shows only two placed efforts from 15 similar runs, so stamping authority from a prominent berth is key.

runners_data.name: Advertised
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 3yo returns after 69 days off and steps back down in trip after two wins over 7f; the lack of recent soft-ground experience is a question mark, though the drop back to 5f and strong early position should suit if fit enough.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose recent form string of 9s and 3s at 5f suggests he needs everything to go right; Nolan takes over and the Good to Soft is not a worry, but Hamilton's straight 5f is a tough track for closers who cannot get a favourable split.

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: One of the more credible late movers here given Cieren Fallon takes the ride and he has a soft-ground win to his name; does best when there is genuine pace to run into and the crowded prominent pack could set this up nicely for his style if he can find daylight.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 3yo ran just two days ago which is a significant freshness concern despite the visor; his two placings on similar going suggest some aptitude, but racing back so quickly after a hard race could blunt his finishing effort here.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner who should lead comfortably under Joanna Mason for the Easterbys; has a 5f course win and handles soft ground, and with no genuine pace duel anticipated she could control the fractions and be very hard to peg back.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 7yo has a strong soft-ground record with two wins in similar conditions over 5-6f, but his natural prominent style means he is unlikely to secure his preferred position in this field-heavy race — he will need to settle for a tracking role slightly further back than ideal, which tempers his chance somewhat.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner whose natural hold-up style means he is genuinely displaced further forward than he would naturally run in this shape; his recent 5f form on good ground is patchy and 5f at Hamilton from an enforced wider position makes this demanding.

runners_data.name: Justmyluck
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 3yo ran only six days ago and wears a hood; the back-to-back racing schedule is a concern and the modest sim-going and form figures suggest she is unlikely to threaten at the business end in this competitive sprint.

runners_data.name: Tatterstall
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' 6yo wears a hood and has a solid recent second at 5f on good ground; a genuine prominent type who should slot in comfortably behind the leader, and a trainer with a 3/27 14-day record suggests quiet but consistent application.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 5yo wears a hood and has run consistently in 5f handicaps with a recent win to his name; Tom Eaves is a sharp booking and the horse's form at this trip on good ground is strong, though the step to soft is an untested variable.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: The field's oldest runner at 10 years but won over 6f on good ground recently and has soft-ground placed form; Jim Goldie runs three here today and Jordan Electrics' hold-up style faces the same headwinds as other closers in what shapes as a pace-dominated race.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo has placed twice on similar going and shown real ability at 5f, but this is naturally a prominent-running horse that will be squeezed for position in this pace-rich field — racing off the pace to some extent limits the scenario in which she shows to best advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Canon's House is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead comfortably from the gates, setting a controlled but honest tempo on Good to Soft ground over this sharp 5f Hamilton track. Vantheman, Germanic, Advertised, Stargazed, and Tatterstall are all genuine prominent types who will press forward behind the leader, creating a bustling early pace that will test anything trying to make ground from off it. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Eternal Sunshine and Parisiac are the most likely to actually slot in just behind Canon's House, with Oriental Prince forced to race further back than ideal. With a strong early gallop likely on softening ground and a field full of pace, the race shape strongly favours horses who can sit within the first four or five and sustain their effort, rather than true hold-up types who will find the ground and pace dynamic working against a late swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Canon's House leads cleanly and the prominent pack race in close order, setting a true-run 5f on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Canon's House dictates from the front, the prominent horses sit just off the pace in ideal stalking positions, and the race is run at a tempo that suits those travelling in the first half of the field from the off; horses with class and the ability to quicken from a handy spot will assert in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Canon's House is allowed to bowl along uncontested and the field fails to reel her in on the softening ground.
scenarios.body: With no horse prepared to commit to chasing hard early, Canon's House controls the fractions and the soft ground masks any lack of true kick, allowing her to last home as pursuers find their ground-eating efforts insufficient.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle burns out and a horse from mid-to-rear produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: With so many prominent types crowding the pace, any leader or close-up horse that over-races in the first half will empty late, opening a slim window for a hold-up horse to thread through; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact Oriental Prince and Justmyluck are not naturally suited to gaining ground at Hamilton over 5f on soft.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos & Crowding
scenarios.trigger: If the large prominent group jostle for position and cause interference, scrambling the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners and multiple prominent types competing for a handful of early positions, a messy break or early crowding could produce a muddling pace that hands an unexpected advantage to a horse able to find a clear run from an awkward position; in this scenario, fresher or less-exposed horses with tactical versatility benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Canon's House — if she gets a clean break and is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, the strong pace dynamic from the chasing pack actually plays into her hands; watch whether anyone commits early to pressuring her or she is simply handed the race on a plate.

Stargazed — ran just two days ago and returned 134lbs; if the horse shows any signs of fatigue or flat-footedness in the early strides it could compromise not just her own run but those racing immediately behind her.

Parisiac and Eternal Sunshine — both are natural prominent types who will be squeezed wide or back from their ideal spot; watch for either being forced into an awkward position at the break which could cause interference for horses behind them.

Sturlasson with Cieren Fallon — the only hold-up horse with a credible soft-ground win, and if the prominent group burn hard through the first two furlongs Fallon will be looking to thread through the gaps approaching the final furlong.

Jim Goldie fields three runners (Oriental Prince, Jordan Electrics, Eternal Sunshine) — worth watching whether there is any apparent stable order or jockey-stable synergy that might hint at which of the three connections feel is their best chance.

races.name: Patersons Of Greenoakhill Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Hunky Dory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who gets a soft lead here — soft ground is a concern given only 1 win from 15 similar-going runs, and the 2-day turnaround is notable; the STYLE_FIT tag suggests her chance should be tempered if she cannot reproduce the sharp form needed to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with back-to-back wins on good ground, David Nolan rides and is adept at Hamilton; soft going is less proven (1 win from 4 similar runs) but the consistent prominent style maps cleanly to the likely race shape.|

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning after a 70-day break for Michael Appleby's yard which fires at 2/18 in 14 days, so the freshness angle is less convincing; has won on similar handicap marks and runs prominently, which suits, but the layoff on soft ground is a genuine query.|

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Jim Goldie whose form reads all placings with no wins in recent starts — the soft ground at Hamilton is not a barrier (soft win in recent history) but the 7f-dominated form over 6f and deep hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong up front.|

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map because the rear is congested — Tim Easterby's runner won on soft ground previously and has soft-ground entries that suggest connections target these conditions, making the style-fit concern the main drag on his chance.|

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent but pushed to midfield on the map because this field has more pace types than available berths — Jim Goldie runner who has placed repeatedly over 6f on good, and the step onto soft ground from good-to-soft form is a mild concern; being denied a natural position will blunt the chance.|

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear — a 3-year-old with no soft-ground wins from 11 qualifying runs, and the recent form of 3-3-3 shows consistent placing without winning; genuinely needs a strong pace to deliver a run-on and that is not guaranteed here.|

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Five-year-old stepping back from 7f-8f trips to 6f, which is a significant distance query — Jim Goldie's yard is active here (three runners) and Rhys Elliott takes the 5lb claim, but the hold-up style and unproven sprint trip make this a difficult assignment in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo.|

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over on this veteran hold-up horse who has a soft-ground place to his name (3rd) — the visor headgear is retained, but a trainer with 0 wins from 6 in 14 days and a form string showing no wins in recent starts make this a watch-from-afar candidate.|

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 6-year-old is a clean prominent type with genuine soft-ground form (4 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-going runs), Tom Eaves who rides regularly here; last run was a handicap win at a similar mark and the prominent style suits this race shape strongly.|

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old natural prominent type whose true position is being denied by a crowded prominent group — the STYLE_FIT discount applies, and the recent form over 7f rather than 6f adds a trip concern; without securing a forward berth this veteran is unlikely to threaten.|

races.paceDynamic: Hunky Dory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap on soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, she is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being dragged into a lung-busting duel. Sir Garfield, Lipsink, and Belsito are natural prominent types who will sit just behind, forming a compact early chasing pack, while the redistribution note is important: Shoot To Kill and Ashen are genuinely prominent horses who are unlikely to find their natural berth in this traffic, and Stirrup Cup and Whiskey Kisses are true hold-up types pushed forward on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded. The field holds considerably more pace and prominent energy than the map can accommodate cleanly — Hunky Dory and the three clean prominent horses (Sir Garfield, Lipsink, Belsito) are most likely to actually secure their positions near the front on the soft Hamilton surface. A sustainable single-pace gallop on soft ground with minimal early pressure favours horses racing prominently who stay on powerfully through the final two furlongs rather than late sprinters, making the prominent-to-lead profile the clear tactical beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Hunky Dory dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo and the prominent quartet press but never truly challenge her early, setting up a one-two from the front.
scenarios.body: Hunky Dory controls fractions on soft ground, the energy-conserving pace allows Sir Garfield, Lipsink, and Belsito to track without burning fuel and mount sustained challenges from 2f out; soft ground rewards those who travel comfortably rather than those grinding from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the soft surface proves more taxing than reported and Hunky Dory's early control costs her late, allowing a prominent horse that travelled smoothly to collar her.
scenarios.body: The leader's early expenditure on soft Hamilton turf catches up inside the final furlong, and a horse like Belsito or Sir Garfield who has been travelling within himself sweeps past; soft-ground stamina and a clean prominent position are the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps because Shoot To Kill or Ashen do push forward and create pressure — to leave a gap for a closer to exploit late.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot early pace would stretch the field and allow a hold-up horse like Abduction or Wreck It Ryley to pick off tiring rivals through the final furlong; however, this scenario depends on horses racing against their redistributed positions materialising, which reduces its likelihood significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Open Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead chaotically and no horse settles into a rhythm, creating a scrambled and unpredictable race shape.
scenarios.body: A lack of early order on soft ground burns out the prominent types, opening the door for an each-way hold-up runner or an unexposed type to emerge; Jannas Journey stepping back from further and Stirrup Cup, a genuine soft-ground winner, are among those to benefit from chaos.

watchPoints.text: Belsito is the most interesting prominent profile — Tom Eaves, Kevin Ryan, soft-ground form of 4W4P from 15 runs, and a recent win; watch whether he can sit second or third and whether he travels smoothly into the straight.

Stirrup Cup is a genuine soft-ground winner but is a true hold-up type placed on the map in midfield — watch whether David Allan pushes him forward or settles for his natural rear position, as that decision shapes the entire back half of the race.

Shoot To Kill and Ashen are both natural prominent horses who may attempt to press forward despite the map redistribution — if either does succeed in getting close to the pace, the early tempo increases materially and the hold-up horses become more relevant.

Sir Garfield's going form on soft is only 1 win from 4 qualifying runs despite dominant recent form on good; watch his early handling of the softer surface as Hamilton's soft ground can expose stamina limitations in a horse whose wins have all come on quicker ground.

Hunky Dory ran just two days ago — monitor the market move and whether Linda Perratt's yard are confident she has recovered sufficiently, as any sign of tiredness late will be exaggerated by the soft conditions.

races.name: Patersons Of Greenoakhill Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Winged Messenger
runners_data.note: Lone pacesetter returning after 56 days, Julie Camacho yard 1/21 in two weeks which is modest, won over this C&D trip on soft before and can control from the front, though his style fit score reflects he is classified as a prominent type rather than a pure tearaway — his tendency to race prominently rather than lead outright may mean he concedes control if tested even mildly.

runners_data.name: City Captain
runners_data.note: 104 days off the track is a concern for fitness sharpness, but Callum Rodriguez provides a booking upgrade and the horse has two soft-ground wins in his recent history over 6f including a C&D victory; prominent style suits this shape well and he arrives on a good profile for the scenario that matters most.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner only 14 days since last run and active in the Goldie yard (4/38 in 14 days), primarily a 5f performer stepping up to 6f again after a poor run over 13th last time at this trip — the drop back to a pace-tracking role on soft ground suits his style but the stamina for 6f on this ground needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has been busy with 5/84 runners in 14 days and David Allan takes the ride on a horse whose true preference is to come from the back; squeezed into a midfield position by the number of natural hold-up types in the field, his one recent soft-ground placing (3rd) is encouraging but the compromised position versus natural style is a material constraint here.

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Won last time out 10 days ago over 6f on good ground, Goldie's second string in the race (Lauren Young claims 5lb), and a natural closer who will be riding closer to the pace than she prefers — the hg:p headgear flag and the recency edge are positives, but Dandy Magic has shown no winning form on soft ground in five similar-going runs and her hold-up style is being crowded by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old dropping in class carrying only 131lbs, one win at 6f on good ground and a soft-ground placing in the book; Rebecca Menzies yard has had no runners in the past 14 days suggesting less live stable activity, but the light weight and Cieren Fallon in the saddle are genuine positives for a horse who races prominently and should find a good position early.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Veteran at eight years old, hg:b (blinkers) fitted and won at 6f on good ground recently, genuinely a hold-up horse by record but forced toward midfield by the field composition — Tristan Davidson is a small operation (1/6 in 14 days) and soft going has not been this horse's friend historically across five similar-going runs with no wins, making the position compromise particularly costly.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: The fade-in-finish flag is a genuine concern on soft ground, with six of his last nine runs resulting in double-figure finishes including two soft-ground efforts where he finished 12th and 6th; David O'Meara busy yard (8/52) sends him here off 28 days, but a true hold-up style that fades late is the worst combination for a soft-ground sprint where stamina is at a premium.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran flagged for fading in the finish and the worst similar-going record in the field with 10 efforts producing no wins and three places; hg:v (visor) worn, 70 days off track, and a soft or heavy surface appears particularly unsuitable based on finishing positions — this profile makes him the most disadvantaged runner in the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: They All Know Me
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey yard are busy (8/39) and David Nolan is a reliable booking, but this horse has been running over 7f-8f in its most recent form and steps back to 6f here — the one soft-ground win came over 7f at Southwell and the natural hold-up style combined with a trip shorter than recent runs makes this a speculative entry relying on others coming back to him.

races.paceDynamic: Winged Messenger is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 6f handicap on soft ground at Hamilton, and with no natural challenger likely to push him from the front, he can dictate a controlled, measured gallop. City Captain, Montezuma, and Daizen are all genuine prominent types who will press to sit just off the pace, creating a compact early order rather than a scorching tempo. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Miraculous, Dandy Magic, and Iris Dancer are true closers by style but will be squeezed into a midfield berth they would not naturally choose, blunting the late-finishing threat each might pose in an ideal scenario. With soft ground slowing proceedings and a single uncontested pacesetter, this race shape strongly favours prominent runners tracking just off Winged Messenger — horses who can hold a good position through the race, avoid the traffic compression from a bunch finish, and produce a sustained run rather than a sharp late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Winged Messenger sets an honest but unhurried tempo and the prominent trackers travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: City Captain and Montezuma, sitting just off the leader, get the softest possible ask through the race and produce sustained runs that the true closers — shuffled forward against their natural style — cannot match for rhythm or timing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly modest and Winged Messenger, never headed and never seriously pressured, simply keeps finding enough on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Soft going rewards a horse who conserves energy in front rather than burning through reserves chasing, and a 56-day freshener may sharpen Winged Messenger's response when his rivals finally throw down a challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Back In Range
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the compact field strings out enough for the hold-up types to find clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: Miraculous has the ability on her best form and Dandy Magic showed a sharp turn of foot winning last time, and if they can navigate from their forced midfield berths into a clear run they become dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish, Any Style Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks chaotically with position-jostling causing traffic problems throughout and no single runner gets a clean run.
scenarios.body: A scrambled finish on soft ground benefits whoever finds the cleanest late passage, and Iris Dancer or They All Know Me — both capable of winning in the right race — could profit from chaos despite being shuffled out of their preferred spots.

watchPoints.text: Winged Messenger's early position is critical — if City Captain or Daizen push him harder than expected in the first furlong, the controlled tempo this race map assumes is disrupted and the whole shape changes.

Dandy Magic and Miraculous are both forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style demands, and if either checks sharply or loses position at the start, they lose what little chance they have in this configuration.

Lord Bertie and Wobwobwob both carry fade-in-finish flags on soft ground at 6f — if the pace quickens at the 2f pole as tired horses stop, these two may create traffic problems for runners on their outside trying to mount genuine challenges.

Daizen's light weight (131lbs) and Cieren Fallon's positive booking deserve monitoring in-running — if the three-year-old travels sweetly just off the pace, his low weight and prominent racing style could see him emerge as a value threat in the closing stages.

races.name: Hemmings Homes 10th Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a recent win on good ground (1/5f/GOO) and only four days since last run, but similar-going record is thin at 0 wins 0 places from 3 runs; the soft Hamilton surface is untested and the closing style is structurally challenged in this shape.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Won on soft (1/6f/SOF) so the ground is not a worry, but the "fades in finish" flag is a real concern over 5f on this going; 39 days off the track is notable, and Jim Goldie's yard is active (4/38 T14), though on soft the tendency to stop late works against a decisive effort.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who can set his own pace, with two wins from two in soft or good-to-soft conditions (1/5f/SOF, 1/5f/GOO) and Joanna Mason adept at making the most of uncontested leads; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects a horse catalogued as Prominent rather than a true leader — temper confidence slightly, but circumstances strongly favour this horse getting the rail and dictating.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Wins at 5f on good (1/5f/GOO) and placed on soft (3/5f/SOF) give reasonable each-way credentials; Conor Whiteley claims 5lb and the horse has placed from a hold-up berth in soft conditions, so there is a small case for a midfield-to-close run if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up veteran whose best recent result came when getting a soft lead (2/5f/GOO) rather than waiting off a genuine pace; true hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map — the STYLE_FIT (0.92) flag suggests he may end up closer than ideal, and recent form (7,6,6,7) on similar ground makes this a tough watch.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Won on good at 5f (1/5f/GOO) but the "fades in finish" flag combined with a natural hold-up style mapped into midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.91) creates a difficult profile; three-year-old in a big handicap field on soft ground, and the most recent soft run ended in a non-completion (U prefix in form string).

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — recent form 489684 reflects a horse that gets involved but cannot sustain the effort; a genuine hold-up runner pushed toward the midfield pack by the race shape (STYLE_FIT 0.92), and no soft-ground wins in five runs gives only limited confidence on the going.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has soft-ground form (5/6f/SOF), and was a recent winner at 6f on good (1/6f/GOO); as a hold-up runner compressed into midfield by the shape of this race (STYLE_FIT 0.93), the shorter 5f trip and this controlled pace makes getting a decisive position difficult despite the headgear angle.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces (tp headgear), trained by Rebecca Menzies with a quiet 14-day record (0/6); 43 days off the track is the key note — seven-year-old without a win in recent 5-6f efforts on good, and no soft-ground wins flagged, though the prominent style suits the race shape.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose best recent finish was 3rd at 5f on good, but similar-going stats are stark (0W 0P from 1 run); placed to midfield on the map (STYLE_FIT 0.92) despite being a natural closer — Jack Garritty rides and trainer Davidson has modest 14-day figures (1/6), making this a marginal contender at best.

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Tim Easterby (very active, 5/84 T14) and ridden by the experienced David Allan — two strong credentials for a tactical horse at a northern track; won at 5f on good (1/5f/GOO) and sits naturally in the box-seat position behind King Of The Jungle, though soft-going win evidence is limited.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist wearing a visor, with placed form at 6f on soft (6/6f/SOF, 3/6f/GOO); dropping to 5f from 6f trips and on soft ground, the Phillip Makin-trained runner has struggled for recent form (006360), but soft-going experience adds a minor argument in extreme scenarios.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style performer with a remarkable placed record (322422 — five places in six) and headgear (b) suggesting focus is maintained; the 5f trip on good is the comfort zone, but soft ground is a query (one 2nd on good at 5f on a standard track), and the Wainwright yard is quietly placed (1/4 T14).

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Jungle is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressure them from the gates, Joanna Mason can dictate terms at a controlled, honest gallop on good-to-soft ground over five furlongs. Tanjen, Kyber Crystal, and Startling will push to grab prominent positions behind, creating a small knot of pressure just off the leader but not enough to turn this into a truly contested, searching pace. The bulk of this field — Harb, Supremissy, Never Dark, Falcon Queen, Doon The Glen, and Jm Jhingree — are natural hold-up horses shuffled toward midfield by the map because there are simply more closer types here than positions allow; in practice, several of them will race closer than their preferred ground due to the moderate pace, which dilutes the advantage of a late run. A controlled-pace scenario on a soft-ground five furlongs at Hamilton historically rewards horses who can sit just behind the leader and produce a sustained, efficient finish rather than a sharp late burst — the prominent-to-midfield profile benefits most, and pure hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Controls, Prominent Profit
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle gets a soft lead and the pace stays honest but not brutal, allowing prominent runners to time their challenge.
scenarios.body: King Of The Jungle dictates from the front without serious pressure, and Tanjen and Startling — sitting in Positions 2-3 — get the perfect cart into the final furlong on softening ground. Prominent types who can race economically behind a lone leader and sustain their effort over the full five furlongs are ideally placed in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle and one of the prominent types — most likely Startling or Tanjen — track closely and the pace is even slower than expected, allowing the front two to steal a march on the field.
scenarios.body: Soft ground compresses the sprint finish and the field struggles to reel in the early movers, meaning horses who are on the bridle in the first two or three positions throughout enjoy a decisive margin. Startling's consistent placed form (322422) and Tanjen's recent course-conditions experience make them the most likely beneficiaries alongside King Of The Jungle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finishers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If a quicker-than-expected early pace causes the front pair to tie up in the final furlong, opening the door for a well-timed run from midfield.
scenarios.body: Hi Lord and Jm Jhingree, though naturally hold-up types, are close enough to the action in a moderate-pace 5f contest to get competitive positions at the two-furlong pole; Hi Lord's soft-ground placed form (7/5f/SOF) is relevant here. This is a minority scenario because the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to truly burn off the leaders on this going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically, compressing the field, and a genuine late-finishing type catches the leaders in the last stride.
scenarios.body: Thistle Nil has a soft-ground win and the fading pattern is a concern, but the horse has prior form on this going; Impressor has soft-ground placed efforts and carries headgear, making it a very marginal live option in an extreme scenario. This shape depends on true hold-up horses finding space through a compressed field, which on a flat five-furlong Hamilton sprint is a low-probability event.

watchPoints.text: King Of The Jungle — if Joanna Mason slots straight to the front unchallenged, the entire race dynamic depends on whether any prominent horse has the will to go with her; watch the first two furlongs to see if the lead is truly uncontested or if Tanjen or Startling apply any pressure.

Tanjen and Startling — both prominent types with valid claims, and if either gets onto King Of The Jungle's quarters from the break, the pace shape intensifies into a genuine contest rather than a controlled procession; David Allan's experience at Hamilton is the key variable to watch at the start.

Supremissy — the "U" (unseated or non-completion) in recent form combined with a "fades in finish" flag on soft ground makes this runner a potential non-stayer in the closing stages; if crowded or hampered in the midfield pack, this horse could cause interference late.

Thistle Nil — 39 days off the track for Jim Goldie, who is active (4/38 T14), suggests the horse may strip fitter than the layoff implies; the soft-ground win on record is the one item that keeps this runner on a shortlist for any reversal, but the tendency to fade late must be factored.

Hi Lord — only 13 days since last run, placed on soft (3/5f/SOF), and jockey Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is live at a track where claims can be decisive in a modest handicap; watch whether the horse gets a clean passage from midfield, as a bunched field on soft ground at Hamilton often produces traffic.
